place.source_title: Charles Olsen Farm, House, Port Oneida

brief: Storey-and-a-half frame farmhouse of the Port Oneida farm community: a steep front gable with a green asphalt roof and a shed wall dormer, a wide front porch with a sunburst-panelled pediment carried on plain columns, clapboard walls with peeling white paint, and a red gambrel barn behind; unoccupied, in a mown field.

facade.notes: the Charles Olsen farmhouse (Port Oneida, Sleeping Bear Dunes, MI, c.1900): a 1.5-storey frame house with a wall dormer, a later porch with a sunburst pediment and segmental arches between columns, windows boarded (in the National Lakeshore); a gambrel barn and a machine shed beyond; mown grass

why.note: farms bought out for the National Lakeshore (1970s): kept, empty
